title: A commit a seat holds is recorded where the push reads it, and no push publishes it until the holder releases it

looked_in: INC-20261018-01: the person's request that e0d09c02 be committed and not pushed lived only in architecture-office-20261016-2's window, so no other seat and no tool could see it at the push that published it

the pushes since HP-009 landed (a65d262e): the pushing seat now asks each owner by message whether a commit is held, which is a round trip per commit per push, and works only while every owner is awake to answer
the commit tool's record, .git/sma-seat-commit.jsonl, which shows that the tool already keeps one shared file outside every tree on this working copy

changes.owner: manager-microscope-office-20261016-1, its builder (shared surface under contracts/)
changes.change: Two modes and one refusal. '--hold <commit> --why <text>' appends a hold to .git/sma-seat-holds.jsonl, outside every tree: the commit, the holding seat (taken from the registry, as for a commit), the time, the reason, and, when the person asked for it, their words verbatim. Only the seat whose commit it is may hold or release it. '--release <commit>' appends the release. A push that would publish a commit with an unreleased hold is refused, whatever --push-includes-others names. The refusal names the commit, its holder and the reason, and the remote stays unchanged. With this, a commit with no hold record is free to publish, and the pushing seat no longer has to ask its owner.

Fixtures: another seat's held commit under the pusher's own is refused even with the exact include list; after release it pushes; a seat cannot hold or release a commit that is not its own; a hold on the pusher's own commit refuses its own push. The first is watched failing on today's tool, which pushes.
One sentence beside the push lines: a commit the person asks to keep local is held with --hold, at once, in the seat's own turn. A hold said in a window and not recorded is not one.

already_running: every seat that pushes: the tool is read from the working copy on each run, and the holds file is read on each push
reach.how_they_learn: A pusher learns from the refusal itself, which names the holder and the reason. A seat holding work learns from the CLAUDE.md sentence and from the tool's usage.

notes: Suggested by architecture-20261003-1, to end the round trips HP-009 made visible. The file is per working copy, as the tool's own log is. A hold protects pushes made from this working copy, and a push from another computer does not see it. That is the same reach as every other gate here, and it is said rather than hidden. Holding is never the tool's own guess: it records what a seat or the person said. No hold record means free, so a hold that is said and not recorded protects nothing. That is why the CLAUDE.md sentence matters as much as the code.
